items.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995
items.q: I got left behind with the Nat Towles’ band... he left us, left me and Henry Coker

ctx.x: No, I got left behind with the Nat Towles’ band many times because Towl would leave sometimes and it wouldn’t be nobody but him. If we was supposed to leave at a certain time he would leave, and he left us, left me and Henry Coker, who later became a great trombone player man, and he left us in DesMoines, Iowa or somewhere. And we went out and picked pockets, somebody picked pockets, and we got our money back and more. I © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -10-

learned. And I tried to pull Coker’s coat you know, because I had seen this happen. You know whatever you say you get pickpocket, you had to make it good, so and I knew this and I had seen this happen you know? So I think we got pickpocket for about $15 apiece, but no money man, you know? So we wake up and everybody’s gone and the money’s gone, and when I went to the landlord of the house and told him that we didn’t have any money and what have you. So he cursed us out and everything. ctx.x: Had you told Hammond about the Nat Tōles -- when you drove up there?

Oh, yeah, we told him about it. We says, 'Can we take you --' We wanted to take him down to -- the next night, we wanted to take ---carry him down to Trenton, New Jersey, where we were playing, but Gatt . . . wouldn't let us off. And he says, 'I can't. I got to be at Bennie's opening tomorrow at the Palomar.' Bennie was opening at the Palomar in Los Angeles. He says, 'I got to be there.' So that night, he went down there and he signed Basie up. So we missed the boat, see, because we had -- our band was in Trenton…
